summary1: I am a software engineer working in field engineering and industrial solutions architecture. I take plants from technical discovery to a live system: workshops, reference architectures, integrations, validation, go-live, and training.
summary2: I'm a Computer Engineering graduate with a Data Science minor from Iowa State University. At Adatafy / Novaspect I have delivered 10 enterprise implementations across pharma, biofuels, campus utilities, food, and chemicals, for sites of 30–150 users.
summary3: The work is usually messy industrial data. I unify MES, historian, CMMS, SAP/ERP, and equipment-log sources across SaaS, on-prem, and hybrid plants, and I resolve the problems that make plant data harder than web-app data: mismatched asset IDs, duplicate events, and historian gaps.
summary4: I also lead the customer-facing technical motion. That includes use-case workshops and roughly 30–40 tailored demos a year for operators, plant IT, validation, and site directors, plus Python and PowerShell deployment automation and TypeScript/Python workflow functions with unit tests and reusable runbooks.
summary5: On the AI side, I build evidence-first industrial agents. PharmaOps Copilot is a CDF-ready pharma deviation-triage prototype: siloed IT/OT/ET exports are contextualized into one model, deterministic tools and hybrid RAG assemble the evidence, and GPT-4, Claude, or Gemini only write the narrative afterward. It ships with 21/21 evals, including jailbreak refusal, plus Industrial MCP-shaped tools and Atlas agents-as-code.
summary6: Earlier, at NVIDIA I built CloudXR demos for medical education stakeholders, and at Dolby I rolled out Agile project workflows that cut cross-team sync meetings and cycle time. I like moving between a plant-floor architecture session and a briefing for the people who have to adopt the system.
